Subject: Follow-up: model routing & policy needs (Acme)

Hi Dev / Marissa / Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great overview of Redwood’s runtime and routing capabilities. To summarize Acme’s top priorities and open questions so we can align next steps: 

- Production constraints: sub-250ms p95 for search assistants, but willing to accept higher for longform generation.
- Cost targets: keep per-1k-token cost under $0.45 for high-volume endpoints (search), explore quantized variants for batch jobs.
- Region requirement: primary service in US, EU for GDPR-sensitive datasets; routing by region is required.
- Fallback behavior: want defined fallback chains (low-latency small model -> higher-quality model -> tenant-fallback to hosted) with circuit-breaker behavior.
- Auth / SDK: need a clear SDK + auth quickstart for our infra team (we use Okta + mTLS for internal services).
- Embeddings / reranker: plan to embed customer content and use a reranker for top-k reordering; want guidance on caching & similarity thresholds.

Can you send a short integration plan (SDK snippets, auth flow, proposed routing policy examples) and propose a follow-up with our infra folks for technical deep-dive? Also attaching our internal mapping doc for context (see acme_mvp_mapping.xlsx).

Thanks,
Sarah
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_mvp_mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the mapping doc. This is exactly what we needed to scope the integration. High-level recap and next steps below.

Recap (short):
- We can meet the p95 latency target for search with a routing policy that pins short-context search to a distilled low-latency model (quantized) and routes longform requests to a higher-capacity model.
- Cost controls: autoscaling + queued batching + prefix caching for frequently-seen prompts will reduce per-token cost.
- Regions: Redwood supports policy-level region routing (route by requester region header + fallback to EU or US zones).
- Fallback chains: we’ll propose a chain: rwd-small-quant -> rwd-medium -> rwd-large-fallback, with circuit-breaker thresholds and a soft-fallback to a hosted SL tier if dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Auth/SDK: we’ll send a quickstart that covers API key + Okta OIDC exchange + mTLS example for private deployment.

Attachments included: redwood_sdk_auth_quickstart.pdf (SDK snippets & auth flow), routing_policy_draft.yaml (example policy).

Action items / proposed owners:
- Dev (me): provide SDK quickstart & sample routing policy by EOD today.
- Marissa: propose model + quantization selection and recommend reranker pattern (embeddings threshold, caching).
- Marcus: schedule infra deep-dive with Acme infra team (Okta / network / mTLS).
- Sarah / Acme: confirm region SLAs (US + EU) and share any procurement timelines.

Proposed follow-up slots for infra deep-dive (30-45m): Tue 11/3 10-11am PT or Wed 11/4 2-4pm PT — tell me what works and I’ll calendar it.

Thanks — I’ll attach the two files in a follow-up and paste the routing_policy_draft inline for quick visibility.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Sarah — adding a few concrete examples and guidance on routing / reranker patterns.

Quick recommendations (ops + quality):
- Routing policy example (summary):
  - Route by request_type: {search, generation}.
  - For search: prefer rwd-search-quant (low-latency) when prompt_length < 512 and client.header.region == "US" or "EU".
  - For generation: route to rwd-std unless cost cap hit, then fall back to rwd-medium-quant.
  - Fallback chain: rwd-search-quant -> rwd-search-medium -> rwd-hosted-std (metrics-based circuit-breaker).
- Circuit-breaker & SLOs: use per-route p95 thresholds wired into autoscaling decisions; trigger fallback when observed p95 > target for 10 minutes and CPU/GPU load > 70%.
- Embeddings + reranker: store vectors in your existing vector DB, use a cached top-100 candidate list per query, run a lightweight reranker (rwd-rerank-small) for final sort. Cache reranker outputs for identical queries for 1h.
- Structured output / tool calling: we recommend using Redwood’s function-calling hooks with explicit schema validation. That reduces downstream parsing errors and enables safe fallback to a text-only model if schema validation fails.

I’ve uploaded the draft routing policy YAML to Drive and attached a local copy for quick review (routing_policy_draft.yaml). Also created a short doc with model recommendations: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-routing-docs

If Acme can confirm the exact p95 target for search (you mentioned "sub-250ms" — is 250ms p95 the strict SLA or a target?), we’ll finalize model picks and quantization levels.

Marissa
Product Lead, Model Serving, Redwood Inference

Attachments: routing_policy_draft.yaml (YAML)
